properties.name: Type 2 Diabetes
properties.definition: The largest group requiring enteral feed will be individuals with type 2 diabetes. Oral hypoglycaemic therapy may be adequate to control glucose, but the combination of insulin resistance associated with acute illness, risk of lactic acidosis or acute kidney injury may mean that their usual medication cannot be used. Metformin can be given as a liquid preparation, via an enteral feeding route. Tablets should not be crushed. If feeding is required urgently then insulin should be used as glucose lowering therapy at an early stage to avoid days of hyperglycaemia associated with oral medication titration. People with type 2 diabetes may have significant endogenous insulin production as well as clinically significant insulin resistance. Large doses of insulin may be required but conversely glucose variability may be less as they may still be making their own insulin. Matching the glucose load to pharmacological activity of the insulin chosen may be less important than for those with type 1 diabetes.
